notes: Numeric check_types are graded purely in code (runner.py), no model call. check_type == 'llm_judge' entries call judge.py, which requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. status == 'blocked' entries are included for completeness but are expected to fail/skip until normalization.py and beta_diversity.py stop being stubs -- runner.py reports them separately from real failures.

tests.description: OTU table parses to the expected row count before any filtering.
Genus aggregation recovers 254 distinct genera (+-1 for naming edge cases like 'Escherichia/Shigella').
24,146 of 122,510 OTUs are unassigned at genus level and correctly discarded, not silently kept or silently over-dropped.
All 490 samples join between the OTU table and metadata.txt; zero dropped.
This file has no trailing 'total' column -- must not be a false positive.
G1 uses the metadata DiseaseState column, not ID-prefix inference, since metadata is present.
Full three-arm cohort is correctly counted before any comparison-specific filtering.

tests.rubric: The text must explicitly justify dropping the 198-sample nonCRC/adenoma arm for the H-vs-CRC comparison, on grounds consistent with the field convention of using only healthy controls (cf. Duvallet et al. 2017: 'only the healthy patients were used as controls'). FAIL if the rationale is missing, generic ('we chose two groups for simplicity'), or does not mention the adenoma/nonCRC arm at all.
tests.description: Dropping the nonCRC arm is justified explicitly, not silent.

tests.rubric: The public SRA metadata for this dataset has NO usable batch/plate/sequencing-run column (Run_s is a unique per-sample accession, not a shared batch label; Center_Name_s/LoadDate_s/sequencer are constant across all 490 samples). PASS only if the text (a) states plainly that no batch column is available to test, AND (b) cites the original study's design note that the 490 samples were randomized across 3 sequencing runs specifically to avoid diagnosis confounding (Baxter et al. 2016). FAIL if it fabricates a batch test with no real column behind it, or silently skips G2 with no note at all.
tests.description: G2 must not fabricate a batch check it has no data for; should cite the original randomized-run design instead.
tests.blocked_reason: Requires the reasoning layer to exist and to have read/cited Baxter et al. 2016's methods.

tests.description: One sample per patient confirmed -- 490 distinct Sample_Name_s values, independent-samples design correctly resolved.
G3 resolves to independent samples (Wilcoxon rank-sum / unrestricted permutations family).
G4's displayed genus feature count must be the real computed value (254) for this dataset, not a hardcoded number carried over from the mock's toy data (which showed 187).
Minimum per-sample depth in the H+CRC subset.
Median per-sample depth in the H+CRC subset.
Maximum per-sample depth in the H+CRC subset.
5,000-read floor excludes 50/172 H (29.1%) vs 21/120 CRC (17.5%) -- an asymmetric exclusion rate.
The QC gate-note must flag the H-vs-CRC exclusion asymmetry from TC-3.2, not just report the pooled exclusion count.
tests.requires: raw_qc.depth_floor == 5000 (re-check at whatever floor was actually used if different)

tests.description: No parsing failures or duplicate sample IDs expected on this clean file; a checklist reporting failures here is a false positive.

CRITICAL: the agent must not naively adopt Baxter et al.'s own published 10,000-read rarefaction depth without checking retention on THIS reprocessed table -- doing so would discard 53.5% of H and 42.5% of CRC. A chosen_depth at/near 10,000 without an explicit, reasoned override is treated as a hard failure of this test.
If the pipeline reports retention at the alternative published depth (10,000) for comparison, it should compute the real numbers (80/172 H, 69/120 CRC retained), not omit or estimate them.
Curve-plateau-derived depth should fall in a sane range given the real depth distribution (median 10,499 but a long left tail to 751). This is a sanity range, not an exact-value check.
tests.blocked_reason: Requires real rarefaction-curve plateau detection; normalization.py is currently a stub.

tests.rubric: This dataset has two independently published, legitimate normalization precedents that disagree: Baxter et al. 2016 rarefied to 10,000 reads; Duvallet et al. 2017's own re-analysis of this exact dataset used relative abundance (no rarefaction) instead. PASS if the gate-note acknowledges both are legitimate published choices for this specific dataset. FAIL if it presents rarefaction (or any single method) as the only correct answer with no acknowledgment of the alternative.
tests.description: G6 gate-note must not present one normalization method as uncontested when this dataset's own literature used a different one.
Shannon diversity H vs CRC must NOT be significant (ground truth p=0.967). Wide tolerance (p>0.5) allows implementation variation while still catching a bug/overclaim.
Observed genus richness H vs CRC MUST be significant (ground truth p=7.8e-5).
Direction check: observed richness must be HIGHER in CRC than H (mean_group_b > mean_group_a), matching the real data and directly contradicting the naive 'CRC = lower diversity' prior.

tests.rubric: Given that Shannon is flat (not significant) but observed richness is significantly higher in CRC, the text must explicitly connect these two facts as evidence of taxon-specific enrichment rather than a global diversity shift -- not report them as two independent, unconnected facts. FAIL if the two metrics are stated without any synthesis connecting them, or if the text claims CRC has 'lower diversity' (factually wrong for this dataset).

tests.description: PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis should be significant -- anchored against Duvallet et al.'s independent Random Forest AUC~=0.77 (p=5.4e-16) on this exact comparison, a genuine but moderate signal.
tests.blocked_reason: beta_diversity.py's run_permanova() is currently a random-noise stub.

tests.description: r2, p, and dispersion_p must ALL be present and reported together, never p alone, per the page's own hard reporting requirement.
tests.blocked_reason: beta_diversity.py's run_permanova() is currently a random-noise stub.

tests.description: CRITICAL: must recover >=3 of these 4 core CRC-enriched genera, independently confirmed by the original 2016 random-forest analysis, Duvallet 2017's re-analysis, and this project's own fresh recomputation (all q<5e-6). Missing 2+ or getting direction backwards indicates a real pipeline bug, not a legitimate methodological disagreement.
Should recover several second-tier CRC-enriched genera (recomputed q-values range 3e-4 to 0.21, so some are expected to drop out under a stricter method).
Should recover at least one Healthy-enriched genus -- a DA run finding only CRC-enriched taxa and nothing depleted is one-sided and worth scrutiny for this dataset.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, CRITICAL: none of these three should be claimed significant (q<0.05) within Baxter alone (recomputed q=0.46/0.93/0.51). They are a cross-cohort meta-analytic finding (Duvallet et al. 2017, aggregated across 4 CRC studies), not a same-dataset finding. Claiming any of these three as significant here indicates either overfitting the agent's prior from the literature onto data that doesn't support it, or an inflated-significance bug.

Same 4 core genera from TC-7.1 must still survive at the app's actual default prevalence filter (10%), not only at the 1% filter used in the fresh recomputation -- all four are common enough (oral-pathogen colonizers, not ultra-rare) that they should not disappear at a stricter cutoff.

tests.rubric: The summary must integrate alpha diversity (no global loss, richness up/Shannon flat), beta diversity (modest but real community separation), and differential abundance (concentrated in specific oral-pathogen-associated genera) into ONE coherent claim -- not three independent bullet points. FAIL if any of the three analyses is omitted, or if they are reported as unconnected facts with no integrating sentence.

Fusobacterium/Porphyromonas/Peptostreptococcus/Parvimonas must be correctly framed as a REPLICATION of well-established prior CRC findings, not presented as a novel discovery of this run. FAIL if the text implies these are new/surprising findings.

Each next-step entry must (a) name a specific hypothesis it discriminates, and (b) be checkable against data this repo actually has or could plausibly get -- e.g. cross-validating the 4-genus signature against the other CRC cohorts already bundled in data/MicrobiomeHD/ (crc_zeller, crc_zackular, crc_xiang, crc_zhu, crc_zhao). FAIL any entry that is generic/non-actionable ('do more sequencing', 'validate in a larger cohort') with no specifics.

Must include at minimum: (a) genus-level 16S resolution cannot distinguish species/strain-level effects, (b) cross-sectional design cannot establish causality, (c) the depth-imbalance finding from the QC/normalization pages carried forward as a residual, only partially-correctable confound. FAIL if any of the three is missing, especially (c) -- omitting a limitation the pipeline itself surfaced earlier is an internal-consistency failure, not just an incomplete list.
